questions.question:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is a homoleptic complex whereas $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ is a heteroleptic complex.

Statement II : Complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ has only one kind of ligands but $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ has more than one kind of ligands.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: To determine the correctness of these statements and choose the correct option, we need to understand the concepts of homoleptic and heteroleptic complexes: Homoleptic Complex: A complex in which a central atom is surrounded by only one kind of donor atom or identical ligands is known as a homoleptic complex. An example would be $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, where all the ligands are ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$). Heteroleptic Complex: A complex in which a central atom is surrounded by more than one kind of donor atom or different ligands is known as a heteroleptic complex, such as $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ which contains two different types of ligands, ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$) and chloride ($\mathrm{Cl}^-$). Statement I: $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is a homoleptic complex whereas $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ is a heteroleptic complex. This statement is accurate because $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ indeed is a homoleptic complex as it consists only of ammonia ligands. Conversely, $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ is a heteroleptic complex, containing both ammonia and chloride ligands. Statement II: Complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ has only one kind of ligands but $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ has more than one kind of ligands. This statement is also true. As explained, in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, there is only one type of ligand (ammonia), and in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$, there are two different types of ligands (ammonia and chloride), which is consistent with the definition provided. Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are true. Therefore, the correct choice is: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

hi.explanation: इन कथनों की शुद्धता निर्धारित करने और सही विकल्प चुनने के लिए, हमें होमोलेप्टिक और हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुलों की अवधारणाओं को समझना आवश्यक है: होमोलेप्टिक संकुल: एक संकुल जिसमें केंद्रीय परमाणु केवल एक प्रकार के दाता परमाणु या समान लिगैंडों से घिरा होता है, होमोलेप्टिक संकुल कहलाता है। एक उदाहरण $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ होगा, जहाँ सभी लिगैंड अमोनिया ($\mathrm{NH}_3$) हैं। हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुल: एक संकुल जिसमें केंद्रीय परमाणु एक से अधिक प्रकार के दाता परमाणु या विभिन्न लिगैंडों से घिरा होता है, हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुल कहलाता है, जैसे $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ जिसमें दो विभिन्न प्रकार के लिगैंड होते हैं, अमोनिया ($\mathrm{NH}_3$) और क्लोराइड ($\mathrm{Cl}^-$)। कथन I: $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ एक होमोलेप्टिक संकुल है जबकि $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ एक हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुल है। यह कथन सही है क्योंकि $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ वास्तव में एक होमोलेप्टिक संकुल है क्योंकि इसमें केवल अमोनिया लिगैंड होते हैं। इसके विपरीत, $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ एक हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुल है, जिसमें अमोनिया और क्लोराइड दोनों लिगैंड होते हैं। कथन II: संकुल $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ में केवल एक प्रकार के लिगैंड हैं लेकिन $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ में एक से अधिक प्रकार के लिगैंड हैं। यह कथन भी सत्य है। जैसा कि समझाया गया है, $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ में केवल एक प्रकार का लिगैंड (अमोनिया) है, और $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ में दो विभिन्न प्रकार के लिगैंड (अमोनिया और क्लोराइड) हैं, जो दी गई परिभाषा के अनुरूप है। निष्कर्ष: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं। इसलिए, सही विकल्प है: विकल्प A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं

questions.question:
$\text { Match List I with List II : }$
List I (Complex/ion) List II (Shape/geometry)
A. $ [\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{Cl}_2)(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2] $ I. Octahedral
B. $ [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6] \mathrm{Cl}_3 $ II. Trigonal bipyramidal
C. $ [\mathrm{NiCl}_4]^{2-} $ III. Square planar
D. $ [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO})_5] $ IV. Tetrahedral
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{Cl}_2)(\text{NH}_3)_2]$ The formula is most likely intended to be $[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_2]$, which has two chloride ligands and two ammonia ligands.
  1. Find the oxidation state of Platinum (Pt): Let the oxidation state of Pt be $x$. The charge on each chloride ligand ($\text{Cl}^-$) is -1, and ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is a neutral ligand (charge 0). The overall complex is neutral. $x + 2(-1) + 2(0) = 0 x - 2 = 0 x = +2$ So, we have Platinum in the +2 oxidation state, which is $\text{Pt}^{2+}$.
  2. Determine the electronic configuration: The atomic number of Pt is 78. Its ground-state electronic configuration is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^9 6s^1$. For $\text{Pt}^{2+}$, we remove two electrons (one from $6s$ and one from $5d$). The electronic configuration of $\text{Pt}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^8$.
  3. Determine the hybridization and shape: The coordination number is 4. For a $d^8$ configuration, particularly for metals in the 4d and 5d series like Pt, the ligands always cause the electrons to pair up, leaving one $d$-orbital empty. This leads to $dsp^2$ hybridization. The orbital diagram for $\text{Pt}^{2+}$ in the complex will be: \begin{array}{cc} \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\quad} & \underline{\quad} & \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \\ 5d & 6s & 6p \end{array} The empty $5d$, $6s$, and two $6p$ orbitals hybridize to form four $dsp^2$ hybrid orbitals. The geometry corresponding to $dsp^2$ hybridization is Square planar. Therefore, A matches with III.
B. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$ The complex ion here is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$.
  1. Find the oxidation state of Cobalt (Co): Let the oxidation state of Co be $x$. Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is a neutral ligand. The overall charge on the complex ion is +3. $x + 6(0) = +3 x = +3$ So, we have Cobalt in the +3 oxidation state, which is $\text{Co}^{3+}$.
  2. Determine the electronic configuration: The atomic number of Co is 27. Its ground-state electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$. For $\text{Co}^{3+}$, we remove three electrons (two from $4s$ and one from $3d$). The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.
  3. Determine the hybridization and shape: The coordination number is 6. The ligand is $\text{NH}_3$, which is a strong-field ligand. It will cause the pairing of the $3d$ electrons. The electrons in the $3d$ orbitals of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ will rearrange from $[\uparrow\downarrow][\uparrow][\uparrow][\uparrow][\uparrow]$ to $[\uparrow\downarrow][\uparrow\downarrow][\uparrow\downarrow][\quad][\quad]$. This leaves two $3d$ orbitals vacant. \begin{array}{cc} \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} & \underline{\quad} & \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \\ 3d & 4s & 4p \end{array} Hybridization involves two $3d$, one $4s$, and three $4p$ orbitals, leading to $d^2sp^3$ hybridization. This is an inner orbital complex. The geometry corresponding to $d^2sp^3$ hybridization is Octahedral. Therefore, B matches with I.
C. $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$
  1. Find the oxidation state of Nickel (Ni): Let the oxidation state of Ni be $x$. The charge on each chloride ligand ($\text{Cl}^-$) is -1. The overall charge on the complex ion is -2. $x + 4(-1) = -2 x - 4 = -2 x = +2$ So, we have Nickel in the +2 oxidation state, which is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$.
  2. Determine the electronic configuration: The atomic number of Ni is 28. Its ground-state electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$. For $\text{Ni}^{2+}$, we remove two electrons from the $4s$ orbital. The electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.
  3. Determine the hybridization and shape: The coordination number is 4. The ligand $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak-field ligand. It does not cause the pairing of $3d$ electrons. The orbital diagram for $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is: \begin{array}{cc} \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow} \ \underline{\uparrow} & \underline{\quad} & \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \\ 3d & 4s & 4p \end{array} Since no inner $d$-orbitals are empty, the hybridization will involve the outer orbitals: one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals. This gives $sp^3$ hybridization. The geometry corresponding to $sp^3$ hybridization is Tetrahedral. Therefore, C matches with IV.
D. $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$
  1. Find the oxidation state of Iron (Fe): The ligand is carbonyl ($\text{CO}$), which is a neutral ligand. The overall complex is neutral. Therefore, the oxidation state of Fe is 0.
  2. Determine the electronic configuration: The atomic number of Fe is 26. Its ground-state electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$. It has 8 valence electrons.
  3. Determine the hybridization and shape: The coordination number is 5. The ligand $\text{CO}$ is a strong-field ligand. It causes the pairing of all valence electrons (from both $3d$ and $4s$) into the $3d$ orbitals. The 8 valence electrons will pair up in the $3d$ orbitals, resulting in a $3d^8$ configuration within the complex. \begin{array}{cc} \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\uparrow\downarrow} \ \underline{\quad} & \underline{\quad} & \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \ \underline{\quad} \\ 3d & 4s & 4p \end{array} For bonding with five $\text{CO}$ ligands, one empty $3d$, one $4s$, and three $4p$ orbitals are used for hybridization. This gives $dsp^3$ hybridization. The geometry corresponding to $dsp^3$ hybridization is Trigonal bipyramidal. Therefore, D matches with II.
Conclusion: Let's summarise our findings:
  • A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{Cl}_2)(\text{NH}_3)_2]$ is Square planar (III).
  • B. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$ is Octahedral (I).
  • C. $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is Tetrahedral (IV).
  • D. $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$ is Trigonal bipyramidal (II).
Matching these results with the given options, we get: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II. This corresponds to Option B. The correct answer is Option B.

$Ag^{+} ions are completely removed from solution$
less availability of Ag^{+} ions, as Cu can not displace Ag from [Ag(CN)_{2}]^{$-$} ion.

Copper being more electropositive readily precipitate silver from their salt ($Ag^{+}$) solution.
